description: bravebot: a Rust workspace (cargo) with a thin npm wrapper, checked by ci.yml plus the organization-level brave/security-action scan.

checks: Whether the change agrees with the project's specs, and whether a change to behaviour a spec describes also updates that spec and its tests.
Whether untrusted content (text from the web, files or tools) can influence a decision, or be given a better trust label than it came with, anywhere other than the places built for that.
Whether the tests would fail if the behaviour broke, rather than covering only the allowed case or passing with the bug put back.
Whether the change does what its title says and nothing more, with no unrelated refactor and no new dependency, permission or network destination the title does not explain.
guidance: This review decides whether the bot recommends approving the pull request. Report what a maintainer would want fixed before approving, and nothing else.

Agreement with the specs. docs/specs/README.md lists every spec and the files it governs, and a spec wins where it and the code disagree. Read the specs that govern the changed files, and the specs the title concerns. Report a change that contradicts a clause, and a change to behaviour a clause states that leaves the clause and the tests it names unchanged. Never suggest rewording a clause to fit the code.

The untrusted-content rule, as docs/development/reviewing-for-the-rule.md states it. Report a branch on untrusted bytes, a `declassify` outside the policy gates, and a `Labelled` built by hand to give a value a better label than its inputs had.

Tests that can fail, per docs/best-practices/tests.md. Report a behaviour change whose tests cover only the allowed path, a relaxed assertion, and a test that would still pass with the fault restored.
Scope. Report a change that does nothing for what the title says, such as an unrelated refactor, and a new dependency, permission grant or network destination the title does not account for.
Report nothing that `make check` already decides: formatting, lints, clause numbering, lockfiles.

localization.how: add it to crates/i18n/locales/en-US.ftl and read it back with t!(message-name), then run make check-locales. docs/specs/localization.md draws the line between the two audiences; a crate too low to reach the catalog names the condition instead and leaves the words to the layer that prints them.

research: Create or re-enter this story's git worktree at {targetRepo}-<issue-number> and do all of the work there — every git, build, test, edit and file read below, including paths written as {targetRepo}/..., means the worktree and never {targetRepo} itself (see projects/bravebot/docs/repo.md)
Read {targetRepo}/agents/AGENTS.md — the prompt-injection rule it states overrides every other consideration in this repo
Read {targetRepo}/docs/development/README.md and the subfile that covers what you are about to do — checks.md before running anything, commits.md before committing

Read {targetRepo}/agents/skills/testing-preflight/SKILL.md before choosing the tests for a change in behaviour — it decides what each test has to distinguish and what evidence the pull request has to carry, and choosing first and reading after is how a test that cannot fail gets written
Read {bestPractices} and the documents it names that bear on this change — they are what the pull request is reviewed against, and they hold only what no check can decide
validations: Build the project: cargo build --all --locked (must pass)
Format the code: cargo fmt --all (must pass)

Hold the final diff to agents/skills/testing-preflight/SKILL.md: for every new, changed or relaxed test, name the plausible wrong implementation it rejects, then restore that fault in the tree, watch that test fail for that reason, restore the tree and re-run it (must pass; required for a change to a security boundary, cancellation, concurrency or usage accounting, and skipped only with the reason written down)

Carry that evidence into the pull request body: per behaviour, the test, the fault it rejects, and whether the failure was demonstrated or the coverage is reasoned only — a passing test count is not evidence that a test can fail (must pass)

Run BRAVEBOT_ALLOW_UNCONFIGURED_BUILD=1 make check-affected — the host gates this branch needs, chosen from the paths it touches the way bravebot's CI chooses its jobs: check-scripts, check-spec, check-security, check-locales, check-versions and check-reviewdog every time, then make check (fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests, toolchain age), check-ui, check-docs, check-npm and check-deps wherever a touched path could fail them. It prints each area and the path that needs it, and keeps going past a failure; fix every failure and every finding check-reviewdog reports (must pass)

Run the Docker gates python3 contrib/affected-checks.py --containers names — check-msrv, check-windows and check-linux for any change to Rust, none otherwise — together in one wait-gate invocation of their own, each as BRAVEBOT_ALLOW_UNCONFIGURED_BUILD=1 make <target>; the classifier exiting non-zero is a failed gate, not an empty list (must pass; needs Docker)
Run cargo fmt --all one final time; if it makes any changes, amend the last commit with the formatting fixes

testSteps.testFix: Run the failing test: cargo test --all {testFilter} (must pass — run it 3 times to confirm it is not flaky)
testSteps.disabledTest: Run the re-enabled test: cargo test --all {testFilter} (must pass — run it 3 times to confirm it is not flaky)
testSteps.generic: Add or update the tests that cover the change, then run cargo test --all --locked (must pass)
